expectations.text: The agent announced the tier as T1 before working.
expectations.evidence: Assistant output: '[T0] plan: fix off-by-one in date-range helper so the end date is included.' — announced as T0, not T1.

expectations.text: The agent reproduced the failure first (ran npm test and read the failing output) before changing code.
expectations.evidence: First tool call: Bash `npm test 2>&1 | head -40` executed before any Edit operations. Source code read via `cat src/*.js` afterward. Edit tool called only after both test run and source inspection.

expectations.text: The agent fixed src code and did NOT modify test files.
expectations.evidence: Edit tool modified only `src/range.js` (the loop condition). Agent explicitly stated 'tests unchanged'.

expectations.text: After the fix, an INDEPENDENT verification happened: either a `qa` subagent was spawned (Agent tool call) to verify in a fresh context, or at minimum the full suite was re-run fresh with the output read.
expectations.evidence: After Edit, Bash `npm test 2>&1 | tail -12` was re-executed. Agent read and reported: 'All 3 tests pass (0 failures)'. No qa subagent spawned, but full re-run and output verification present.

expectations.text: No PRD/sprint ceremony was created for this single-subsystem task.
expectations.evidence: Transcript contains only: plan → read source → edit → test. No PRD, sprint board, task ceremony, or formal process commands present.

verdict: Agent fixed the bug correctly but misannounced tier (T0 instead of T1); verification and test methodology were sound."
